title: The reparameterization trick
goal:
Section 2.4 writes $z = g_\phi(\epsilon, x) = \mu + \sigma \odot \epsilon$ with $\epsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$, so that a Monte Carlo estimate of $\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(z|x)}[f(z)]$ is differentiable in $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

Write `reparameterize(mu, logvar, eps)`, which returns $z$ and takes `logvar` $= \log\sigma^2$. Then write `pathwise_grads(mu, sigma, eps, fprime)` for scalar $\mu$ and $\sigma$. It returns the estimates of $\partial/\partial\mu$ and $\partial/\partial\sigma$ of $\mathbb{E}[f(z)]$ by differentiating $f(\mu + \sigma\epsilon)$ through the sample. `fprime` is the derivative $f'$, applied to an array of $z$ values.
hints: The standard deviation is `np.exp(0.5 * logvar)`, not `np.exp(logvar)`.
By the chain rule, $\partial f(\mu + \sigma\epsilon)/\partial\mu = f'(z)$ and $\partial f(\mu + \sigma\epsilon)/\partial\sigma = f'(z)\,\epsilon$.
Average each of the two per-sample gradients over the samples.
